channel.title: Crypto Front Page
channel.description: Crypto Front Page reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, exchanges, DeFi protocols, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto industry.

item.title: How to bridge crypto during a sharp market move
item.description: During a sharp move, check the route, final amount, fees, settlement path and destination gas before bridging; urgency can make a slow or thin route costly.

item.title: Coinbase and Marqeta pair stablecoins with card payments
item.description: Marqeta and Coinbase will let enterprise customers offer stablecoin-funded cards, pairing Coinbase custody and conversion with Base settlement and Marqeta processing.

item.title: What Wallet Swappers Should Check for Price Impact and Slippage
item.description: Price impact is built into a swap quote; slippage is the change before execution. Check both, plus minimum received, route, fees and network.

item.title: Estimate Wallet Changes Across Two Chains
item.description: Estimate cross-chain wallet change by rebuilding balances per chain, separating transfers from bridge flows, and checking which addresses can be linked with confidence.

item.title: Bridge or Swap: How to Choose Between Them
item.description: A bridge moves an asset between chains, while a swap changes the asset; compare route, fees, timing and destination needs before choosing, and check what arrives in your wallet.

item.title: Why a Bridged Token May Not Appear in Your Wallet
item.description: A bridged token can be absent because the transfer is unfinished, the wallet is on another network, or the destination token needs to be added by contract address.

item.title: Bridge funds first, then deploy a smart account on Mantle
item.description: A Mantle smart account can receive bridge funds before its contract exists, but deployment, gas payment and the bridge recipient must line up on Mantle.

item.title: How to Send Tokens to an Escrow on Another Network
item.description: Cross-network escrow uses a bridge to lock or burn tokens, verify the transfer, and credit a destination contract; the route and escrow terms must match.

item.title: Why Mantle Bridge Transfers Can Fail at the Destination
item.description: A Mantle transfer has separate source and destination steps; checking each chain’s transaction, recipient and token contract helps locate what failed.

item.title: How a treasury can fund a falling health factor
item.description: A treasury can restore a falling health factor by repaying borrowed tokens first, then adding eligible collateral, while keeping liquidity for fees and further price moves.

item.title: Why a Destination Chain Rejects a Crypto Transfer
item.description: A destination chain rejects a transfer when its address, transaction format or fee rules fail validation; the failure point determines whether it waits or returns.

item.title: Why Mantle Bridge Transfers Show as Separate Wallet Transactions
item.description: Wallet history records each side of a bridge separately: the source-chain send, the destination-chain arrival, and any later withdrawal steps.

item.title: Replenishing Collateral After a Network Migration
item.description: After a network migration, collateral returns only when the right asset reaches the supported chain and is supplied to the lending market; balances do not move automatically.

item.title: How to Reconcile Cross-Chain Treasury Transfers
item.description: Cross-chain treasury reconciliation matches each source-chain debit to its destination-chain credit, accounting for fees, timing, and transfers still in flight.

item.title: How Partial Fills Meet Cross-Chain Swap Minimums
item.description: Partial fills let a swap execute in pieces, while cross-chain minimums set the least acceptable destination output; learn how to compare both before signing.

item.title: When a Sequencer Stops Mid-Bridge
item.description: A sequencer outage can pause one leg of a bridge after the source transaction lands; what happens next depends on the bridge design and recovery path.

item.title: How to Verify a Treasury Transfer Across Chains
item.description: A treasury transfer is complete only when the source debit, bridge message and destination credit agree on asset, amount, recipient and final status.

item.title: Why Bitcoin Arrives on Ethereum as a Wrapped Token
item.description: Bitcoin reaches Ethereum as a token backed by BTC held elsewhere, so it can enter smart contracts with added bridge, custody and redemption risks.

item.title: How to Estimate a Cross-Chain Swap Output
item.description: A cross-chain swap estimate starts with the source amount, then subtracts route fees and price impact to predict what should arrive on the destination chain.

item.title: Ledger says implant sent wallet recovery phrases over LTE
item.description: Ledger says an implant inside CryptoBilis-sold wallets read 24-word recovery phrases at setup and sent them over LTE, exposing funds without breaking the secure chip.
